findings.title: Negative-offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on Django querysets
findings.body: The 'advanced features' branch does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django ORM querysets do not support negative indexing — slicing with a negative start raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported in querysets`. The comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false. Any request that reaches this branch (cursor with negative offset, `optimized_pagination=true`, privileged user) will produce a 500 instead of a page of results. Since cursors are client-supplied strings parsed by `Cursor.from_string`, a negative offset is trivially craftable, making this a denial-of-service on the endpoint.

findings.title: BasePaginator now slices with unclamped negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The original code did `queryset[offset:stop]` and the new code does `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, then slices. For non-prev cursors the `max(0, offset)` clamp prevents negative offsets, but for prev cursors the raw (possibly negative) offset is passed straight to queryset slicing. Combined with `Cursor.from_string` accepting any integer offset from the client, a malicious cursor such as `0:-5:1` on any endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses will hit Django's negative-slicing AssertionError (or, for list-backed paginators, silently return wrong rows). This changes behavior of every existing BasePaginator consumer, not just the new 'optimized' path, and is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by datetime
findings.body: The audit log endpoint sorts by `-datetime` and previously used `DateTimePaginator`, which converts datetimes to epoch-millis ints for cursor keys. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` is copied from the plain `Paginator` and does `int(math.floor(value) if ... else math.ceil(value))` on the raw attribute; when the attribute is a `datetime`, `math.floor`/`int()` raise `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware...`/`type error`. So the optimized path crashes whenever it needs to compute an item key (any request with results). Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value, whereas `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` converts the millis value back into a timezone-aware datetime for the SQL comparison — the optimized path would compare a float against a datetime column and break the query. The paginator is simply not usable for this endpoint's data type.

findings.title: zpopmin eviction silently drops buffered spans with no metric or cap configurability
findings.body: The new eviction block pops `span_count - 1000` members off the set whenever a segment exceeds 1000 spans, permanently dropping those span payloads before they are ever flushed to the `buffered-spans` topic. The Python-side `max_segment_spans` guard (which skipped the segment and logged an error) was removed from `_load_segment_data` without replacement. The 1000 limit is hardcoded in Lua, is inconsistent with the Python `max_segment_spans = 1001` default, and there is no metric increment, log, or counter when eviction occurs — segments above 1000 spans will be silently truncated, making the data loss invisible in monitoring. Eviction also uses `zpopmin` (lowest end timestamp), meaning the oldest spans of a segment vanish, potentially including the root/segment span that later code (`is_segment` detection, redirect handling) depends on.

findings.title: Redis structure changed from sets to sorted sets without migration handling
findings.body: The script now calls `zcard`/`zunionstore` where it previously called `scard`/`sunionstore`. During a rolling deploy, old-version processes still write span payloads via `sadd`/`sunionstore` while new-version processes read them with `zcard`, so existing set-typed keys are invisible to the new logic (`zcard` on a set key returns a WRONGTYPE error in Redis, actually failing the EVALSHA call entirely). There is no migration or versioning strategy, so deploying this will produce errors/data loss for any in-flight traces buffered before the deploy. `buffer.py` also changed `sadd`→`zadd` and `sscan`→`zscan` symmetrically, but mixed-version operation during rollout is not handled.

findings.title: Redirect traversal limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The redirect-following loop bound was cut from 10000 to 1000 with no explanation in the PR description and no constant shared with Python. The original comment noted the limit means segment trees of depth 10k may not join correctly; reducing to 1000 tightens that failure mode. If a redirect chain exceeds 1000 hops, the loop exits with `set_span_id` pointing at an intermediate node and the span is written to the wrong buffer key, splitting a segment — silently, since the returned `redirect_depth` metric is the only signal. If this reduction was intentional (e.g. to bound Redis script runtime), it should be documented and covered by a test; neither exists.

findings.title: Undocumented, untested query-parameter-gated paginator switch on a control-silo endpoint
findings.body: A new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter changes which paginator implementation and behavior (including negative-offset support) the audit log endpoint uses, but it is not documented in the API schema, not covered by any endpoint test, and the behavior difference is invisible to clients. The permission gate uses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` (owner/manager) or superuser, but audit logs are sensitive security data and the 'advanced' path offers no clear benefit while introducing the crash bugs above. This change is also entirely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (span buffer optimization), making it easy to miss in review.

findings.title: paginate() may not forward enable_advanced_features to the paginator constructor
findings.body: The call passes `enable_advanced_features=True` to `self.paginate(...)`. Whether this kwarg reaches `OptimizedCursorPaginator.__init__` depends on the endpoint base class's `paginate` implementation forwarding arbitrary kwargs to `paginator_cls`; the standard `paginate` in sentry's API base constructs the paginator with a fixed set of arguments (queryset, order_by, etc.). If it does not forward the kwarg, this raises a TypeError (500) on every optimized request; if it does forward it, the default `enable_advanced_features=False` still enables the negative-offset branch only for this flag combination, which no test exercises. Either way there is no test covering this endpoint's new code path.

findings.title: No tests for eviction, oversized segments, or the new sorted-set behavior
findings.body: The core behavioral changes of this PR — segments exceeding 1000 spans being truncated via `zpopmin`, the removal of the `max_segment_spans` guard in `_load_segment_data`, and the set→sorted-set conversion — have no test coverage. All existing tests use tiny traces (4-5 spans) with identical timestamps, so they cannot catch wrong sort scores, eviction of the wrong members, or eviction of the root span. A test that builds a segment of >1000 spans with distinct `end_timestamp_precise` values and asserts which spans survive is needed before this data-lossy change can be merged.

findings.title: Pre-existing typo `order_b` means ASC conversion of descending order_by never applies
findings.body: In `build_queryset`, the branch that converts an existing `-{key}` ordering back to ascending assigns to `queryset.query.order_b` instead of `queryset.query.order_by`. While pre-existing, the new negative-offset/OptimizedCursorPaginator work sits directly on top of this path and the diff touches the surrounding function, so the bug now affects the new paginator too: a prev-cursor request on a queryset already ordered by `-datetime` will not have its ordering flipped to ASC, producing incorrectly ordered (and thus incorrectly paginated) results. Worth fixing while this code is being modified.
